title: Higher dairy prices threaten yogurt-melt margins.
evidenceFor: Advertised yogurt products create a plausible solids-cost channel.
evidenceAgainst: Pass-through, contracted inputs and actual category contribution are unknown.
indicators: Milk/solids quotes; product contribution; pass-through lag
falsification: No material margin change across two sustained >10% input-price moves.

title: Premium pet spending increases demand for freeze-dried toppers.
evidenceFor: Advertised toppers align with a substantial pet category.
evidenceAgainst: Dollar spend can reflect inflation; premium units and Watershed order mix are unknown.
indicators: Segment units; launches; briefs; conversion to orders
falsification: Three periods of segment growth with no comparable qualified lead/order response.

title: Drought in a key fruit origin affects Watershed within 60 days.
evidenceFor: Fruit processing establishes a possible channel.
evidenceAgainst: No key source region or inventory cover is verified.
indicators: Verified origin; drought; crop yield; contracted cover
falsification: Verified sourcing lies elsewhere or contracted supply/cover prevents a measurable 60-day effect.

title: Popcorn expansion adds corn, oils, cheese-powder, film and promotion exposures.
evidenceFor: Announced popcorn transition and process growth.
evidenceAgainst: Commissioning, actual formulas and customer terms remain unknown.
indicators: Operating milestone; formulas; packaging specifications; retail promotion orders
falsification: No production transition or relevant ingredients/formats in the confirmed portfolio.

title: Top Fox creates differentiated seed and roasting exposure.
evidenceFor: Seed products and the brand’s farming origin are public.
evidenceAgainst: Origins, owned vs bought inputs and manufacturing allocation are unknown.
indicators: Food-grade seed harvest; origin concentration; roasting yield
falsification: Verified production and input model has no incremental seed/roasting exposure.

title: Automation lowers labor exposure but raises OT and specialized-maintenance dependency.
evidenceFor: Maintenance and engineering are public capabilities.
evidenceAgainst: Automation intensity and measured labor productivity are unknown.
indicators: Labor hours/unit; maintenance delays; software inventory; vendor dependency
falsification: Automation adds no measurable labor saving or dependency after controlled comparison.
